paragraphs: Chapter 1021
Episode 247. Liberation War of Laprarosa (9)
Swoosh-!
Shimat quickly closed the distance with Jin, leaving a trail behind. The reddened Tetallon drew a flash between Jin and Shimat.
Until just now, his sword bore the desperate struggle of those driven to despair, but not anymore.
Having broken the ancient chains of the Sun God and destiny, he had become a completely different person. It wasn’t just his body that had changed, but his inner self as well.
A sense of liberation only known to those who have broken free from long chains.
His inner self was free from impurities like regret or remorse. In a way, he was directly confronting a destiny of destruction.
Receiving his punishment, his life coming to an end.
Such things were mere secondary issues. What mattered was to not lose the fighting spirit until the end.
To meet his end not as a follower of the Sun God or a dog of fate, but as a member of the 'Red-Name Tribe.'
"Kaaa!"
Clang-!
Shimat roared as he repelled Sigismund. The spikes of lightning that sprang up along Sigismund's trajectory pierced through Shimat's abdomen, but physical harm was meaningless now.
Shimat's body was merely the shape of a person crafted from red energy, the real body had already turned to ash and scattered across the battlefield.
That’s why Ban had said so. It's easy to end a life, but not so easy to kill a will.
So strong.
Even the unique fighting style supported by the air fortress might have been just another chain, he thought.
In fact, Shimat was advancing, and Jin was retreating while parrying his sword.
'I never dreamed I would see Brother Jin fighting while retreating after merging with a Battle God.'
'Has he become like those devils, transcending physical laws? We are almost done here; maybe I should assist him before Brother Jin gets even a little hurt.'
The Battle Kings thought.
Bakarun, Bekios, Rakiman. The Grand Battle Kings of the Red Plutonian were barely breathing, hiding from Murakan and the Battle Kings around the battlefield.
[Even though he said not to worry about the Battle God, their eyes seem uneasy.]
Murakan immediately read the minds of the Fighting Kings.

"Hmm! Perhaps the fusion with the Battle God isn’t in a perfect state right now. It would be painful if Brother Jin gets seriously injured. He is still a Genesis, after all. Besides, it seems like he has awakened something right now."
Murakan shook his head at Belize's words.
[You're talking without knowing much.]
"Why?"

[If you interfere unnecessarily, you'll get hurt. You are strong, but that fight is on a completely different level. Then, the kid will be in danger trying to protect you. In my eyes, the kid still has an overwhelming advantage. Thanks to that guy Ban's senses. So, it’s better for you to conserve your strength.]
"Conserve our strength?"

[Surely, those scoundrels will swarm here. Those who sowed this chaos... Veil went to call Luna and Runtia, right? We should use our strength to deal with those bastards. That's why I'm not helping the kid. The kid is probably saving the last move of that tremendous sword for the same reason.]
Just like Murakan said, he deliberately didn't interfere in the battle between Jin and Shimat. It was time to prepare for a new threat.
[Must feel invincible. Like there's nothing in the world that can't be beaten, even me or the Battle God brothers.]
The reason Jin seemed to be retreating was precisely what Murakan had mentioned. In a way, Jin was 'moderately' dealing with Shimat.
There was no need to use too much power to extinguish Shimat, who was already destined to die, to break his will.
"What kind of nonsense is this, Jin Runkandel! Is it not fun to fight with me? It won't be easy to find a rival like me in your lifetime. Don't regret it after today, better to fight properly."
[But Shimat, your awakening is... utterly meaningless to me.]
"What?"

[You might be happy to be liberated from fate, but I have no reason to empathize with that sentiment. Shimat. You threatened me and my comrades, threatened the world, and desperately tried to prevent my brothers from seeing the light of the world again.]
Jin stepped on Shimat's foot and thrust his blade towards his throat. Shimat did not dodge the sword but counterattacked instead. Tetallon grazed past Jin's eyes.

[As a warrior, it's not that there's nothing in you that I can respect, but that's all it is. You don't deserve to see the end of my sword. We are never friends or the like. I cannot respect any part of your barbaric will and ideology.]
It was an utterly unexpected story for Shimat.

"Ah, you seem to be worried about Kri. More fearful than expected. Of course, if that had been there from the beginning, the situation would be different now. It would have been difficult for me to break down barriers like now. But our technology has its limits. It's impossible to break through this confusion and request support with Critil. So, Kri won't be coming."
[That would be your perspective.]
Shimat's pupils widened.
- What do you expect from me?
- You haven't even mentioned the purpose of your visit yet?
- You must have come to tell me how to interfere with the Barmel Alliance and the descendants of Blue Plutonian. Tell me what you want."
- Ah, if it's about what I want... I don't particularly want anything.
Suddenly, a conversation he had with Rokia came to mind.
"Hehe, right. Thinking about it, that makes sense. The witch, and Rokia Ganesto. Those guys wouldn't have just left our base alone."
The strongest war weapon of the Red Plutonian, Kri.
Jin was now more conscious of Kri than Shimat. After all, it was not the Barmel Alliance, the Red Plutonian, Ziffle, Kinzelo, but Ganesto who had unleashed chaos in the great desert.

'Stealing Kri would be entirely possible with the powers and abilities Rokia Ganesto possesses. There's likely no one in the Red Plutonian’s base capable of dealing with the Ganestos right now. Especially if Rokia Ganesto himself makes a move.'
Jin had never directly experienced the extent of Rokia Ganesto's power.
However, Rokia had already encouraged Shimat to use chaos. Even without ever appearing in the great desert.
'Surely, Rokia will lead Kri here. He must have planned this from the start. Shimat and the Red Plutonian will be defeated, and my comrades and I won't be able to leave the great desert.'
Leaving the great desert now would mean Shimat would naturally perish over time, but it would leave Lafrarosa unprotected.
'Brother Jin, we've secured the device you sent us. Brother Boras understood how to use it right away.'
'Understood, brother.'
For the next twelve hours, Jin had to protect Lafrarosa, no matter what came his way. And now, Jin had the power to do so.

[Using the power of chaos was a clear mistake. Don't expect an honorable death, Shimat. You're just a foolish leader who led yourself and your people into a trap, into the jaws of chaos. It would be a stroke of luck for your kind if you could die intact.]
"I see you have no intention of fighting me properly. But can you keep that up?"
Suddenly, Shimat started to rush past Jin.
Jin didn't miss the moment Shimat started to run. He stabbed his sword into Shimat's back, but he didn't stop.
He was aiming for Lafrarosa.
[Kid, I'll handle the main cannon of the air fortress, just focus on him!]
[Shimat, using such shallow tricks... ]
"It seems you're still not angry enough. If I finish off a few more of your brothers with my own hands, that relaxed face of yours will have to distort."
Just before Shimat's sword energy reached Lafrarosa, Jin raised his hand and activated the lightning energy of Plutonian’s  Domination Sword in that direction.

Following Jin's will, the thunder energy spread like a tidal wave in an instant, intercepting Shimat's sword energy. However, Shimat didn't miss the opportunity and sliced Jin's right arm, causing blood to spurt.

"No matter how transcendent your power, you are ultimately a mortal made of bone, flesh, and blood. If you're struck at a vital point even once, you'll die. On the other hand, I might be temporary, but I'm as good as immortal. Wouldn't it be better for you, Jin Runkandel, to simply cut me down instead of being distracted trying to protect your brother?"
It was a cowardly and shallow tactic.
However, it was the awakened Shimat who was employing this tactic. Even Jin, merged with the fighting god, couldn't take him lightly.
Moreover, he had to conserve strength in anticipation of other enemies, so Shimat had made the best decision.
'This is a bit tricky. But no problem. He can’t even scratch Lafrarosa. I’ve already confirmed the limit.'
Just as Jin thought this and was about to push Shimat back with another surge of thunder energy.
Boom!

All four of the airborne fortresses simultaneously fired their cannons. Naturally, Murakan thought it was aimed at Lafrarosa and tried to expand the dark arrival as a shield to cover against the enemy's cannon.
But the target of the four cannons wasn't Lafrarosa.
The cannons hit exactly where Shimat had been pushed back and fell due to the blue thunder energy. Before he could regain his composure, he was buried under the bombardment fired by his own people.
"What?"
Just like when he was stabbed and slashed by Jin's sword several times, the red shadow-like body didn't transmit pain to Shimat.
But Shimat was engulfed in a shock worse than being torn and melted away, incomparable to anything else.
"My people, what is this..."
Even if the outer armor was completely torn and the inside severely damaged, there's no way the cannons would miss their target. Shimat knew this better than anyone.
Clearly, the cannons fired by his people were aimed at him.
'Betrayal? No, no... my people wouldn't betray me. Then, this must be.'
Chaos, undoubtedly the work of Ganesto.
It felt as though a black blade was swirling in his head. Shimat barely managed to evade the bombardment and looked up at the sky where the air fortresses were, with trembling eyes.
First, he saw the damaged fortresses in an unfamiliar state. Above them, the sky darkened as a portal to the dimension of chaos opened.
The sight of the fortresses exiting that portal and converging towards a war weapon, which the Red Plutonians had always been most proud of, followed.
It was the air fortress of the Battle God, Kri.
